faqs.a: Value Added Tax (VAT) is a consumption tax added at each stage of production, but the consumer ultimately pays it. In the UK the standard rate is 20%; Saudi Arabia and the UAE charge 15% and 5% respectively; India uses GST (a similar system) with rates of 5%, 12%, 18%, and 28%.

When you remove VAT, you divide by (1 + rate), not subtract the percentage. Removing 20% from £120: 120 / 1.2 = £100, not £96. Subtracting 20% from £120 gives the wrong answer (£96) because the original 20% was calculated on the £100 net price.
faqs.q: Why can't I just subtract 20% to remove VAT?

faqs.a: The UK VAT registration threshold is £90,000 of taxable turnover in a rolling 12-month period. Below that, registration is voluntary. Voluntary registration lets you reclaim VAT on expenses but forces you to charge VAT to customers - worth it mainly for B2B businesses.
faqs.q: When must a UK business register for VAT?

faqs.a: VAT is a European-style tax charged on value added at each stage; GST (Goods and Services Tax) is India's unified version of the same idea. Both are ultimately paid by the end consumer. The maths in this calculator works identically for both.
faqs.q: VAT vs GST - what is the difference?

faqs.a: Yes - many items have reduced or zero rates. In the UK: 5% on domestic energy, 0% on most food, books, and children's clothes. Saudi Arabia applies 15% broadly with limited exemptions. Check your country's tax authority for the exact rate on your item.

vat-calculator.formula:
Adding VAT: gross = net x (1 + rate).
VAT amount = net x rate.
Removing VAT: net = gross / (1 + rate).
VAT amount = gross - net.
Example (20%): removing from 120 -> 120 / 1.2 = 100.
howTo: Choose Add VAT (you have the net price) or Remove VAT (you have the gross price).
Set the VAT rate (20% is the UK standard, 15% Saudi, 5% UAE).
Read the net price, the VAT amount, and the gross price instantly.
keyFacts: UK standard VAT is 20%; reduced 5% on energy, 0% on most food, books, and children's clothes.

Removing VAT means dividing by 1.2 (at 20%), not subtracting 20% - a common and costly mistake.

Businesses can usually reclaim the VAT they pay on expenses from the tax authority.

vat-calculator.quickAnswer: Removing 20% VAT from £120: net price is £100, VAT is £20 (120 / 1.2 = 100). Adding 20% VAT to £100: gross is £120. Never just subtract 20% from the gross - that gives the wrong answer. The UK standard rate is 20%, Saudi Arabia 15%, UAE 5%.

vat-calculator.workedExample:
£120 including 20% VAT:
1. Net = gross / (1 + rate) = 120 / 1.2 = £100.
2. VAT amount = 120 - 100 = £20.
3. Check: 100 x 20% = £20, and 100 + 20 = £120. Correct.
Wrong method: 120 - 20% = £96, which is wrong because the 20% was charged on the £100 net price, not the £120 gross.
